fix: (1) A continuation/salvage lane's audit MUST diff its deliverable against the ORIGINAL rejecting audit's machine-readable defect list (the evolve-verdict JSON already carries defects[]) and emit per-defect dispositions FIXED/DEFERRED(where)/OPEN — an audit that cannot account for a named defect cannot PASS the continuation. (2) Retro-filed remediation items must be written to .evolve/inbox transactionally with the retrospective (not only into the report). (3) A closure claim in CHANGELOG/bookkeeping ships must cite the per-defect disposition artifact. Wiring proof mandatory for each. DOCS REQUIRED (operator directive 2026-08-04): the landing must include/extend an issue/gap/solution section in docs/operations/batch-integrity-review-2026-08-04.md (or a linked doc in the same format).
notes: Adversarial batch review 2026-08-04. Also queue the triage protected-surface admission check separately (sank cycles 1257, 1259, 1263 — three full lanes).
summary: Proven arc: 1255 audit FAILs with D1-D4 -> 1268 salvage reframes -> 1270 fault-localization says 'already fixed upstream' -> retroactive ACS renames the task to its fixed subset -> 1272 CHANGELOG seals 'verified closed'. D1(b)/D4 vanished; separately 1267-F2/F3 and 1259-D5/1263-D3 (triage keeps committing protected-surface tasks — named twice as 'highest-value fix available') were named-then-never-queued. Root causes: (1) continuation lanes verify the SALVAGE's framing, not the REJECTING audit's defect list; (2) retro-filed items can live only inside retrospective-report.md and never reach the inbox (lesson-to-action-gap live instance); (3) CHANGELOG closure claims are unverified prose.
title: Salvage/continuation chains launder rejected defects: each hop re-frames scope and named CRITICALs vanish from every tracking surface
